title: Finite surjections with open local lifts dominate fppf coverings
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes [def-weil-size-convention], quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a small fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site], meaning that the $f_i$ are flat, locally of finite presentation and jointly surjective. Then there exist a surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] finite morphism $p:X'\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and a small open covering $X'=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U'_\alpha$ [def-weil-open-immersion], such that for each $\alpha$ there are an index $i(\alpha)\in I$ and an $X$-morphism $U'_\alpha\to X_{i(\alpha)}$. No flatness of $p$ is asserted. The empty scheme and its empty covering are allowed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fppf-integral-surjective-refinement] to the given fppf covering. This gives an integral surjection $q:Y\to X$ and open subschemes $W_\alpha$ covering $Y$, each equipped with an $X$-morphism $h_\alpha:W_\alpha\to X_{i(\alpha)}$. The lemma applies to the full small family; no quasi-compactness of the $X_i$ is required.

An integral morphism is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Thus $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), and $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2), since $X$ is so. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], for every $y\in W_\alpha$ choose an affine open neighbourhood contained in $W_\alpha$. These form an open cover of $Y$; quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] selects finitely many, denoted $V_1,\ldots,V_r$. Each $V_j$ lies in one selected $W_{\alpha(j)}$; restrict $h_{\alpha(j)}$ to obtain an $X$-morphism $a_j:V_j\to X_{i(j)}$. In particular, each $V_j$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

Use [lem-weil-pbc-integral-morphism-limit-of-finite] on $q$ to write $Y=\varprojlim_\lambda Y_\lambda$ as an inverse system over a nonempty directed set, with projections $\pi_\lambda:Y\to Y_\lambda$, affine transition maps, and finite finitely presented structure morphisms $p_\lambda:Y_\lambda\to X$, satisfying $p_\lambda\circ\pi_\lambda=q$. Each $Y_\lambda$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: finiteness implies affineness by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], affine morphisms are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) applies over $X$.

Apply clause (1) of [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] to each quasi-compact open $V_j\subset Y$. A common upper bound of the finitely many resulting indices gives a stage $\lambda_0$ with quasi-compact opens $V_{\lambda_0,j}\subset Y_{\lambda_0}$ whose inverse images are $V_j$. Quasi-compactness is preserved when moving to this common stage by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open], since transition maps are affine and hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). For $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$ let $V_{\lambda,j}$ be the inverse image of $V_{\lambda_0,j}$. Clause (3) of [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] exhibits $V_j=\varprojlim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_0}V_{\lambda,j}$ with quasi-compact stages and affine transitions. The stages are also quasi-separated: the affine opens of the open subscheme $V_{\lambda,j}$ cover it by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and they are affine opens of the ambient scheme $Y_\lambda$, so their intersections are quasi-compact by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion], and clause (2) gives the assertion.

The descended opens must still form a covering after increasing the stage. Set $B_{\lambda_0}=\bigcup_{j=1}^rV_{\lambda_0,j}$. This is a quasi-compact open, since from any open cover of this finite union one selects a finite subcover on each of its finitely many quasi-compact constituents [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Both $B_{\lambda_0}$ and $Y_{\lambda_0}$ have inverse image $Y$ in the limit, because the $V_j$ cover $Y$. Apply the eventual-equality clause (2) of [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] to these two opens. At some $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_0$ their inverse images agree, so $Y_{\lambda_1}=\bigcup_jV_{\lambda_1,j}$. Every later stage also has this covering, by taking inverse images.

For each $j$, the target $X_{i(j)}\to X$ is locally of finite presentation by the given fppf-covering hypothesis [def-pc-fppf-site]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-map-limit-factorization] over the fixed base $X$ to the restricted limit $V_j=\varprojlim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_0}V_{\lambda,j}$ from step 4 and the map $a_j$. Its hypotheses hold: these stages are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, their transitions are affine, and $a_j$ is an $X$-morphism. Hence for some $\mu_j\ge\lambda_0$ there is an $X$-morphism $b_j:V_{\mu_j,j}\to X_{i(j)}$ whose pullback along the limit projection is $a_j$. This uses only local finite presentation of the target, not quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $X_{i(j)}$.

Choose a common upper bound $\lambda$ of $\lambda_1$ and all the finitely many $\mu_j$, and put $X'=Y_\lambda$, $p=p_\lambda$ and $U'_j=V_{\lambda,j}$. The maps $U'_j\to V_{\mu_j,j}\xrightarrow{b_j}X_{i(j)}$ are $X$-morphisms; the first map is the restricted transition morphism. The opens $U'_j$ cover $X'$ by step 5. Finiteness and finite presentation of $p$ are the properties already supplied in step 3. For every $x\in X$ choose $y\in Y$ with $q(y)=x$; then $p(\pi_\lambda(y))=x$, so $p$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. This proves all conclusions, with the finite and hence small index set $\{1,\ldots,r\}$.

If $X$ is empty, take $X'=X$ and $p=\operatorname{id}_X$ with the empty open covering. The identity is finite (on every affine chart its coordinate algebra is generated by $1$ as a module), finitely presented (the algebra presentation has no generators or relations), and surjective; its diagonal is an isomorphism, so the quasi-separatedness in finite presentation also holds [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. There are no indices or lift maps to choose. Thus an empty original indexing set causes no exception: joint surjectivity then forces $X$ empty [def-pc-fppf-site]. All other constructions take place in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], enlarging the auxiliary universe if necessary, and the delivered open cover is finite. No flatness of $p$ has been used.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_surjective_fppf_refinement {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] {I : Type u} (Xi : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : (i : I) → Xi i ⟶ X) [hflat : ∀ i, Flat (f i)] [hlfp : ∀ i, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f i)] (hjoint : ∀ x : X, ∃ i y, f i y = x) : ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (p : X' ⟶ X), IsFinite p ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation p ∧ QuasiCompact p ∧ QuasiSeparated p ∧ Surjective p ∧ ∃ (A : Type u) (U : A → Scheme.{u}) (j : (a : A) → U a ⟶ X'), (∀ a, IsOpenImmersion (j a)) ∧ (∀ a, ∃ (i : I) (g : U a ⟶ Xi i), g ≫ f i = j a ≫ p) ∧ (∀ x : X', ∃ a y, j a y = x)
